words.meaning: ıssız doğa, kırsal alan, Avustralya çalılığı
sentences: She grew up in the bush and moved to the city for university at eighteen.
He went for a walk in the bush on Sunday morning and saw a kangaroo.
The bush stretches for hundreds of kilometres beyond the last town on the highway.
She loves the smell of eucalyptus that fills the air when walking through the bush.
He found living in the bush peaceful but sometimes lonely during the long winter months.
The bush was dry and crispy after months without any significant rainfall.
She volunteered with a bush regeneration group on weekends to restore native vegetation.
He photographed a tiny blue-tongue lizard sunning itself on a rock deep in the bush.
The bush is home to an extraordinary diversity of plants and animals found nowhere else on Earth.
She packed water, a map, and a charged phone whenever she ventured into the bush alone.
He drove through the outback from Adelaide to Alice Springs and was humbled by the scale.
She had never experienced such silence until she camped alone in the outback.
The outback covers a vast portion of Australia's interior with sparse human settlement.
He needed a satellite phone when travelling through the outback because there was no mobile reception.
She prepared carefully for the outback crossing — extra fuel, water, and emergency supplies.
The red dirt and ochre rocks of the outback are a striking contrast to the coastal cities.
He spotted a road train carrying cattle across the outback highway — it was enormous.
She was overwhelmed by the number of stars visible in the outback sky away from any light pollution.
Outback communities rely on the Royal Flying Doctor Service for medical emergencies.
He gained a deep respect for the land and its Traditional Owners during his outback journey.
She monitored the bushfire alerts on the RFS app during the hot and windy summer day.
He evacuated his property after the bushfire warning was upgraded to emergency level.
The bushfire season in Australia typically runs from October through to March.
She kept a go bag ready during bushfire season so the family could leave within minutes.
He volunteered with the Rural Fire Service and spent many days fighting bushfires.
The bushfire destroyed thousands of hectares of national park and dozens of homes.
She checked the fire danger rating on the Bureau of Meteorology website each morning in summer.
He cleared the gutters and trimmed trees near the house as part of bushfire preparation.
The 2019–2020 Black Summer bushfires shocked Australia and much of the watching world.
She found the smoke from distant bushfires irritating to her lungs even forty kilometres away.
The region endured a severe drought for three consecutive years with little rainfall.
She grew up on a farm and remembered the hardship her family faced during the long drought.
The drought forced many farmers to destock their properties and sell livestock at low prices.
He designed a water-efficient garden specifically suited to drought conditions.
The drought restrictions limited residents to watering gardens only twice a week.
She donated to a rural aid organisation helping farming families through the devastating drought.
He installed a rainwater tank to reduce dependence on town water supply during drought periods.
The drought broke after steady rainfall in autumn — the relief in farming communities was visible.
She wrote a school project about the economic and emotional impact of drought on Australian farmers.
He noticed the creek near his property had dried up completely — a stark sign of drought.
She evacuated her Lismore home after authorities warned the flood was set to reach record levels.
He volunteered to fill sandbags for neighbours whose homes were threatened by the flood.
The flood damaged the ground floor of the house completely — furniture and floors were ruined.
She checked the bureau of meteorology flood warning map before crossing the causeway.
He learned the hard way never to drive through floodwater — the current was stronger than expected.
The flood relief fund raised millions of dollars from Australians around the country.
She was offered temporary accommodation by the council while her house dried out after the flood.
He photographed the high-water mark on the fence post left behind after the flood receded.
Eastern Australia experienced devastating floods multiple years in a row in the early 2020s.
She reviewed her home insurance policy to confirm it included flood cover after the event.

words.meaning: sıcak hava dalgası, kavurucu yaz dönemi
sentences: She stayed indoors with the air conditioning on during the four-day heatwave.
He checked on his elderly neighbours every morning during the heatwave.
The heatwave pushed temperatures above forty-five degrees in parts of South Australia.
She filled a spray bottle with water to cool down during the heatwave at the outdoor event.
He moved his elderly cat's bed into the coolest room of the house during the heatwave.
The council opened cooling centres at libraries for residents without air conditioning.
She drank at least three litres of water a day throughout the week-long heatwave.
He cancelled the outdoor birthday party after the heatwave forecast showed forty-two degrees.
Heatwaves are the deadliest natural hazard in Australia, causing more deaths than any other disaster.
She followed the bureau's heatwave warnings closely and planned all outdoor activity before nine AM.

words.meaning: UV (morötesi ışın) indeksi, güneş yanma riski ölçeği
sentences: She checked the UV index on the weather app before deciding to take the children to the park.
The UV index reached eleven — extreme — so they stayed indoors until after three in the afternoon.
He had not realised the UV index could be high even on overcast days in Australia.
She applied sunscreen whenever the UV index was three or above, as recommended.
The UV index in Australia is among the highest in the world due to the ozone layer.
He taught his children to check the UV index each morning as part of their sun safety routine.
She downloaded a UV alert app that sent a notification whenever the index reached three.
The UV index can reach dangerous levels as early as nine in the morning in summer.
He was surprised the UV index was six in the middle of winter — still high enough to cause damage.
She referred to the SunSmart guidelines which recommended protection whenever the UV index was three or above.
She applies sunscreen SPF 50+ every morning before leaving the house regardless of season.
He kept a tube of sunscreen in his work bag for lunchtime walks during summer.
Australia has one of the highest rates of skin cancer in the world — sunscreen is essential.
She reapplied sunscreen every two hours while spending the day at the beach.
He bought a sport sunscreen that stayed on better during sweaty outdoor activities.
The school sent a note home reminding parents to apply sunscreen before school during summer.
She found a sunscreen that doubled as a moisturiser — perfect for her daily routine.
He learned too late about sun damage — his dermatologist now checks him every six months.
Sunscreen should be applied fifteen to twenty minutes before going outdoors for best protection.
She used SPF 50+ sunscreen on the children and made sure they wore hats and rashies at the beach.
He got a bad sunburn at the cricket and his shoulders were peeling for two weeks.
She treated her sunburn with aloe vera gel from the chemist to soothe the irritation.
Sunburn can occur in as little as eleven minutes in Australia during peak UV hours.
He did not think he would get sunburn on a cloudy day — but he was very wrong.
She warned her overseas visitors about how quickly sunburn happens in the Australian sun.
He missed one spot on his back with the sunscreen and got a perfectly shaped sunburn outline.
Repeated sunburn significantly increases the risk of developing skin cancer later in life.
She applied sunscreen carefully on the children to prevent painful sunburn at the outdoor concert.
He visited his GP after noticing a suspicious spot that had started as a bad sunburn.
Sunburn is a sign that UV damage has already occurred — prevention is always better than cure.

words.meaning: Avustralya'nın güneş koruma sloganı: giyin, sür, tak (gömlek, güneş kremi, şapka)
sentences: She grew up hearing slip, slop, slap on every summer ad and still follows it every day.
He repeated slip, slop, slap to his children as they packed for a day at the beach.
Slip, slop, slap was introduced by the Cancer Council in the 1980s and transformed sun safety habits.
She explains slip, slop, slap to overseas colleagues who are unfamiliar with Australian sun safety.
The slip, slop, slap message has since been extended to include seek shade and slide on sunglasses.
He used slip, slop, slap as a checklist before any outdoor activity with the family.
She pinned a slip, slop, slap reminder on the school noticeboard at the start of each term.
He credited slip, slop, slap education at school with his lifelong habit of using sunscreen daily.
The slip, slop, slap campaign is considered one of the most successful public health campaigns in history.
She reminded her visiting parents about slip, slop, slap before their first Australian summer day.
She spotted a mob of kangaroos grazing at dusk on the edge of the nature reserve.
He slowed down on the rural highway after seeing a kangaroo warning sign.
The kangaroo bounded across the paddock with remarkable speed and grace.
She took her overseas visitors to a wildlife park where they hand-fed kangaroos.
He read that kangaroos are most active at dawn and dusk — the most dangerous driving times.
The eastern grey kangaroo is the most commonly seen species in parks along the east coast.
She watched in delight as a joey poked its head out of its mother's pouch.
He was surprised by how large a large male red kangaroo could be — almost two metres tall.
Kangaroos are a protected species in Australia — harming one without a permit is illegal.
She found kangaroos in the backyard of her regional property perfectly normal.
She spotted a koala wedged high in a eucalyptus fork during her walk through the national park.
He learned that koalas sleep up to twenty hours a day to conserve energy from their low-nutrient diet.
Koalas are listed as vulnerable in Australia due to habitat loss and disease.
She visited the koala hospital in Port Macquarie and was moved by the care the animals received.
He was lucky enough to see a koala with a joey on its back in a tree near the campsite.

She noticed a koala slowly crossing the road and stopped traffic in both directions.
He read that chlamydia is a significant health challenge in many wild koala populations.
Koalas have a very specific diet — they eat the leaves of only a small number of eucalyptus species.
She donated to a wildlife charity that plants eucalyptus corridors to support koala populations.
She found a wombat grazing near the campsite at dusk and watched quietly for several minutes.
He was surprised by how solid and stocky a wombat was — almost like a small furry boulder.
Wombats produce distinctive cube-shaped droppings which they use to mark territory.
She learned that wombats are excellent diggers and create extensive burrow systems underground.
He almost tripped over a wombat crossing the path in the dark at the campground.
Wombats are nocturnal and most active during the cooler hours of evening and early morning.
She took her children to see the wombat enclosure at the wildlife sanctuary.
He read that a wombat's pouch opens backwards so dirt does not enter while digging.
The southern hairy-nosed wombat is found primarily in arid regions of South Australia.
She was charmed by the wombat's slow, lumbering walk — it had a very endearing quality.
She heard a possum on the roof at night and initially thought something was very wrong.
He spotted a ringtail possum curled up in the shrubs in the backyard.
Possums are very common in Australian suburban gardens, even in major cities.
She called a wildlife carer when she found an injured possum on the footpath.
He installed a possum box in the garden tree to give the neighbourhood possum a safe home.
The possum had been eating her tomatoes — she moved the pot plants inside to protect them.
She learned that possums are protected and cannot be relocated without a permit.
He watched the common brushtail possum pick up a piece of fruit with surprising dexterity.
Possums are more vocal than expected — their hissing and screaming can be startling at night.
She found a joey clinging to a deceased possum and called a wildlife rescue line immediately.
She found an echidna curled into a defensive ball by the side of the walking track.
He slowed the car to a stop when an echidna waddled slowly across the country road.
The echidna is one of only two egg-laying mammals in the world — the other is the platypus.
She watched the echidna use its long sticky tongue to extract ants from a small mound.
He had never seen an echidna in the wild before — he was thrilled when one appeared near the campsite.
Echidnas have powerful digging claws and can bury themselves rapidly when threatened.
She learned that a baby echidna is called a puggle — she found that delightfully charming.
He photographed the echidna from a respectful distance without disturbing it.
Echidnas are found across Australia and New Guinea in a wide variety of habitats.
She explained the difference between an echidna and a hedgehog to her visiting British cousin.
She wore a helmet on her morning bike ride to protect herself from swooping magpies.
He learned that magpies only swoop during nesting season — roughly August to October.
The magpie song at dawn is one of the most distinctive and beautiful sounds in Australia.
She drew eyes on the back of her helmet after reading it deterred magpies from swooping.
He made friends with the local magpie by feeding it scraps — it now comes to the back door daily.
The magpie is widely considered one of the most intelligent birds in the world.
She warned her new neighbour about the swooping magpie nesting near the letterbox.
He watched three magpies cooperate to mob a much larger bird of prey overhead.
Australian magpies are not closely related to European magpies despite the similar name.
She downloaded a magpie attack map app to plan the safest walking route during swooping season.
She was woken by the kookaburra's laughing call at sunrise — it was an unforgettable sound.
He spotted a kookaburra perched on a fence post staring at the barbecue with great interest.
The kookaburra call echoing through the bush is one of the most iconic sounds in Australia.
She taught the children the kookaburra nursery rhyme on the camping trip.
He was amazed when the kookaburra dove from its branch and caught a small snake instantly.
Kookaburras mate for life and live in family groups that defend shared territories.
She heard kookaburras calling in the late afternoon before a summer storm — a natural alarm.
He left a small piece of meat on the rail — the kookaburra swooped down almost immediately.
The kookaburra is a member of the kingfisher family and is native to eastern Australia.
She listed the kookaburra as her favourite Australian bird — the laugh was too joyful to resist.

words.meaning: galah (pembe göğüslü kakadu); aynı zamanda aptal anlamında argo
sentences: She saw a flock of galahs tumbling across the sky — their pink and grey feathers glowing in the sun.
He laughed when his grandfather called someone who made a mistake a complete galah.
Galahs are among the most widespread parrots in Australia and are instantly recognisable.
She stopped the car to watch a large flock of galahs feeding on seeds in a paddock.
He kept a galah as a pet for fifteen years — they are intelligent and love human interaction.
The galah flew into the tree and immediately started hanging upside down to show off.
She used galah in a sentence as a good-natured insult and her Australian friend grinned.
Galahs form large flocks and can be extremely noisy during the early morning hours.
He noticed the grey galahs were male and the pink ones were female — he had it backwards.
She photographed a galah perched on a fence post at sunrise with the paddock stretching behind it.
She heard the sulphur-crested cockatoo before she saw it — the screech was unmistakable.
He watched a flock of cockatoos strip every piece of fruit from the backyard tree overnight.
The white cockatoo raised its bright yellow crest in alarm when the dog came too close.
She photographed a black cockatoo — a less common but spectacular sight in the bush.
He was warned that cockatoos can cause serious damage to wooden structures with their beaks.
The cockatoo wolf-whistled at her from the pet shop window and she could not help laughing.
She read that cockatoos can live up to eighty years and form very strong bonds with owners.
He spotted a pair of red-tailed black cockatoos — a rare find that made his year.
The sulphur-crested cockatoo is one of the most recognisable birds on the Australian continent.
She found the screech of a hundred cockatoos roosting in the suburb thoroughly deafening.

He watched a rainbow lorikeet hang upside down from a banksia flower to extract nectar.
Rainbow lorikeets are among the most vividly coloured birds found in coastal eastern Australia.
She was surprised that lorikeets eat nectar and pollen rather than seeds like most parrots.
He photographed a pair of lorikeets grooming each other high in the branches of a grevillea.
The lorikeets descended on the bottlebrush outside her window every afternoon in summer.
She read that feeding lorikeets bread or honey can cause health problems — stick to proper mix.
He startled a flock of lorikeets which exploded from the tree in a burst of colour and noise.
Lorikeets are very social birds and are rarely seen alone in the wild.
She identified the scaly-breasted lorikeet at the park — slightly less common than the rainbow.
She planted native species in the garden to attract local birds and reduce water use.
He learned that native grasses are better suited to Australian soils than imported lawn varieties.
The council encourages residents to replace exotic plants with native alternatives.
She admired the native wildflowers that covered the hillside after the autumn rain.
He asked the nursery staff for recommendations for native plants suited to a shady courtyard.
Native animals are protected under Australian law and cannot be kept without a permit.
She joined a bush regeneration group that replaces invasive weeds with native seedlings.
He identified a native violet growing through the cracks of his garden path.
Native vegetation provides critical habitat for insects, reptiles, and birds.
She chose native ground cover plants for the verge — they needed no watering once established.
Foxes are an invasive species introduced to Australia in the nineteenth century for hunting.
She volunteered on a project to control invasive species threatening the local wetland habitat.
He read that cane toads are one of the most destructive invasive species in Australian history.
Invasive species cost the Australian economy billions of dollars in damage each year.
She learned that lantana is a highly invasive plant species smothering native bushland.
He helped remove invasive weeds along the creek bank as part of a community restoration day.

She was surprised how many familiar garden plants are actually classified as invasive species.
He reported a sighting of an invasive species to the local biosecurity officer.

She called a wildlife rescue line after finding an injured bird beside the road.
He was careful to keep his dogs leashed near bushland to avoid disturbing native wildlife.
Australia's wildlife is unique — many species are found nowhere else on the planet.
She donated regularly to a wildlife sanctuary that rehabilitated injured animals.
He slowed down at dusk knowing wildlife was most active and likely to cross the road.
The wildlife corridor connects two patches of bushland allowing animals to move safely.
She watched a documentary about Australian wildlife and was amazed by the diversity.
He joined a community group that installs nest boxes to support local wildlife.
Wildlife photography is a popular hobby among nature lovers across Australia.
She found the wildlife camera footage from the backyard — a possum and a bandicoot in one night.
She studied conservation biology at university and went on to work for a national park.
He supported a conservation charity working to protect the endangered regent honeyeater.
Conservation efforts have helped some threatened species begin to recover their numbers.
She volunteered for a conservation program that monitors turtle nesting sites each summer.
He spoke at a community meeting about the importance of conservation in the local catchment.
Conservation groups campaigned to protect the old-growth forest from logging.
She chose eco-friendly products and practices as her personal contribution to conservation.
He explained conservation principles to primary school children during an environmental incursion.
The national park was created to ensure conservation of the unique ecosystem for future generations.
She applied for a grant to fund conservation research on a critically endangered frog species.
She hiked through the Blue Mountains national park and was awestruck by the Three Sisters.
He camped in the national park for four nights and saw more wildlife than he could count.
National parks in Australia protect some of the most extraordinary landscapes on earth.
She paid the entry fee at the national park gate and received a printed map of the trails.
He found the national park website invaluable for planning the route and checking conditions.
Campfires may be prohibited in national parks during high fire danger periods.
She reminded her children to leave no trace while walking through the national park.
He was moved by the ancient ochre handprints in the cave shelter inside the national park.
The national park ranger led a guided walk explaining the ecology of the local bush.
She bought a national parks annual pass — it paid for itself after the third visit.
She snorkelled above the reef and was mesmerised by the colour and diversity below.
He learned about the threats facing the Great Barrier Reef and decided to donate to reef research.
The reef provides habitat for thousands of species of fish, coral, and other marine life.
She chose reef-safe sunscreen before entering the water near the coral ecosystem.
He took a glass-bottom boat tour over the reef and watched a sea turtle glide beneath him.
The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef system in the world — visible from space.
She was saddened to see sections of the reef that had been bleached by warming ocean temperatures.
He volunteered for a citizen science program monitoring coral health on the reef.
The reef supports billions of dollars in tourism revenue for the Australian economy annually.
She educated her children about protecting the reef by never touching or standing on coral.
She was devastated to read the news about another mass coral bleaching event on the Great Barrier Reef.
Coral bleaching occurs when water temperatures rise and stress the coral, causing it to expel its algae.
He learned that coral can recover from bleaching if temperatures return to normal quickly.
Scientists recorded the worst mass coral bleaching event in history in 2024.
She explained coral bleaching to her students using a simple classroom demonstration.
He chose a reef-safe sunscreen to avoid contributing chemicals that can worsen coral bleaching.
Coral bleaching does not kill the coral immediately — but repeated events weaken and eventually kill it.
She donated to a foundation funding research into coral bleaching resilience and recovery.
He was moved by underwater footage showing the ghostly white landscape of bleached coral.
Reducing carbon emissions is considered the most critical step in preventing further coral bleaching.
She walked through the Daintree rainforest and felt like she had stepped back in time.

The rainforest was cool and misty even on the hottest summer days on the coast.
She identified an enormous strangler fig tree growing at the edge of the rainforest track.
He spent the afternoon photographing fungi, insects, and birds in the rainforest.

She felt humbled by the sheer scale and age of the trees in the ancient rainforest.
He read that the rainforest in north Queensland is home to species found nowhere else on earth.
The rainforest provides clean water for communities downstream through natural filtration.
She planned a family trip to the rainforest to experience its extraordinary biodiversity.

He was amazed by the number of frogs calling from the wetland on a warm, wet evening.

He read that wetlands store significant amounts of carbon — protecting them helps the climate.
The wetland was listed under the Ramsar Convention as a wetland of international importance.
She brought her school class to the wetland for an environmental education excursion.

He carried five extra litres of water for the desert crossing — exactly as the ranger recommended.

She taught her children to recycle from a very young age by sorting rubbish together.

He read the council recycling guide to make sure he was sorting correctly.
She found a recycling drop-off point at the supermarket for soft plastics.
He recycled the old printer at an e-waste drop-off point rather than sending it to landfill.
She checked the recycling symbol on the packaging before deciding which bin to use.
He attended a community talk about what can and cannot be recycled in their local council area.
She bought products made from recycled materials whenever a good option was available.

He set up a worm farm on the balcony as an alternative to a full outdoor compost system.

He learned that coffee grounds and tea bags are excellent additions to a compost system.
She checked the compost temperature to make sure it was breaking down properly.
He asked the council whether food scraps could go in the green organic waste bin for composting.
The compost was ready after three months — dark, earthy, and perfect for the garden beds.
She shared her compost surplus with neighbours who had no space for their own bin.
He was surprised how much food waste his household produced once he started composting.

words.meaning: yeşil çöp kutusu (organik atık: bahçe ve yemek artıkları)
sentences: She put the lawn clippings and vegetable peelings into the green bin on collection day.
He checked with the council whether cooked food scraps could go in the green bin.
The green bin is collected fortnightly in her council area and processed into compost.
She put the weeds in the green bin rather than the compost to avoid spreading seeds.
He ran out of space in the green bin after a big weekend of gardening.
The council newsletter explained that meat and dairy should not go in the green bin.
She labelled the three bins clearly — green for organics, yellow for recycling, red for general waste.
He appreciated that the green bin collected food scraps and garden waste in a single service.
She tracked the green bin collection schedule on the council website so she never missed it.
He noticed his household's general waste bin was barely full since starting to use the green bin properly.

words.meaning: sarı çöp kutusu (geri dönüşüm: plastik, kağıt, metal, cam)
sentences: She flattened the cardboard boxes before placing them in the yellow bin.
He rinsed the glass jars before adding them to the yellow recycling bin.
The yellow bin accepts paper, cardboard, glass, cans, and hard plastics in most councils.
She made sure the yellow bin lid was fully closed on a windy bin night.
He read the council guide to confirm which plastics were accepted in the yellow bin.
She was annoyed when a neighbour put a bag of rubbish directly into the yellow bin.
He put the empty milk cartons in the yellow bin every collection week.
The yellow bin is collected weekly in his council area while the general waste is fortnightly.
She separated food from packaging before adding anything to the yellow bin.
He taught his children that soft plastics like bags do not go in the yellow bin.
She is passionate about sustainability and applies its principles in every area of her life.
He chose an employer that had a genuine commitment to environmental sustainability.
Sustainability means meeting today's needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs.
She gave a presentation on sustainability initiatives at the school environmental committee.
He bought from brands that demonstrated credible sustainability practices and transparent reporting.
Sustainability encompasses environmental, economic, and social dimensions — not just recycling.
She reduced single-use plastics at home as one practical step toward sustainability.
He found sustainability fascinating as a university subject — the challenges are enormous but solvable.
The company published its annual sustainability report outlining progress toward emissions reduction goals.
She discussed sustainability with her children over dinner and was inspired by their questions.
